newsitem.title: THAILAND: KR Precision bids on IBM contract. [CORRECTED 00:50 GMT 29/11]
newsitem.headline: KR Precision bids on IBM contract. [CORRECTED 00:50 GMT 29/11]

text.p: Thai hard disk suspension manufacturer KR Precision said on Wednesday it has bid on a an IBM contract for 500,000 hard disk assemblies a week, worth 10 million baht.

"IBM has asked us to quote and we have put in an aggressive bid. If we are successful, and we are confident that we will be, then we will start shipping in the second quarter of 1997," John Sullivan, KRP's vice-president of operations, told Reuters.
Thailand's Board of Investment said earlier it granted IBM tax incentives to invest over 14 billion baht ($560 million) to build two hard disk drive plants in Thailand's eastern provinces.

If it wins the bid, KR Precision would resume supplying existing IBM sub-contractor assembler Saha Union with components for standard IDE interface hard disk drives prior to the completion of IBM's new plants.

Sullivan said KRP has not supplied components to IBM since 1995 and said the success of this deal opened up a strong possibility that IBM would use KR Precision as its primary supplier in Thailand once its new facility was ready in 1998. (Corrects to clarify that KR Precision could only be IBM's primary supplier in Thailand, not globally).
"If they like the price we will ship them pieces for evaluation. We expect to a decision within two or three weeks," Sullivan said.
He said IBM's decision to expand its presence in Thailand offered KR Precision a sizeable advantage over competitors because of its proximity.

Current main suppliers of suspensions for IBM drives are said to be America's Hutchinson Technology International and NHK Precision of Japan. Sullivan said IBM was estimated to consume 120 million drive suspensions in 1996 worldwide. (Corrects to show the figure is the amount of drive suspensions IBM will consume, not produce, globally in 1996).
KR Precision shares closed up 8.0 to 163 baht on Wednesday, against an overall rise in the Thai market of 0.11 percent.
